heroHeadline: Trump-Xi Summit Day 2: Xi Warns Taiwan Mishandling Could Trigger War; Both Agree Hormuz Must Stay Open; Trump Invites Xi to White House September 24; Warsh Confirmed Fed Chair 54-45
heroSubtitle: On May 14, 2026 (Day 475 of the Trump era; Day 75 of the US-Iran war), President Trump and President Xi Jinping held formal bilateral sessions at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on Day 2 of the first US presidential visit to China in nearly nine years. Xi warned Trump directly that mishandling Taiwan would put the US-China relationship 'in great jeopardy' and could lead to 'clashes and even conflicts.' Critically for the Iran crisis, both leaders agreed the Strait of Hormuz 'must remain open,' with Xi expressing interest in purchasing more US oil and both affirming Iran can never obtain a nuclear weapon — a joint declaration interpreted as Beijing aligning with Washington to apply indirect economic leverage on Tehran. Brent crude dipped ~$3 to ~$107.82/bbl on the Hormuz agreement news. Trump invited Xi to visit the White House on September 24. Scott Bessent signaled a Boeing mega-aircraft-purchase deal is being neared. Jensen Huang (Nvidia) joined Elon Musk in the CEO delegation. On the domestic front, the Senate confirmed Kevin Warsh as Federal Reserve Chair in a 54-45 vote on May 13 — the narrowest modern-era confirmation and first fully partisan Fed Chair confirmation — succeeding Jerome Powell whose chairmanship expires May 15; Warsh's first FOMC meeting as Chair is June 16-17.
